unverifiable: The preregistration protocol has several holes. The git-order test covers only results/<M>/, but outcomes also live in gen/M2 (evidence.json, sorts/, diagram/), laws/<M> (derive output: I20 predicts basis counts), replay/ and spec/M2/disagreements.json. Uncommitted local runs before the prereg commit cannot be detected. Per-key immutability of spec/M2/predictions.json is not checked. The test sits in tests_m2, which is agent-editable and unfrozen. It cannot be a gate check, because tests/_util.copy_repo drops .git, and skipping when .git is absent would be a 'make tests skip' violation.

Many preregistrations restate outcomes already observed: I1 P1/P2, I4 statuses, I6, I21 'reproduce M1 outcomes', the I22 back-test, I25 'L_tag_BVH keeps its outcome', I27's frontier with (1000,0) dominated (already in docs/M1_REPORT.md §2.1), and I3's coverage counts. Counting them inflates the §13/L8 prediction-accuracy metric. They should be filed as regression expectations, not predictions.

M2 exit (a), '0 unexplained disagreements', can be met by labelling: spec/M2/disagreements.json is agent-written. Each class needs a mechanical criterion: extraction_defect means fixed and re-run green; real_defect means linked to a REFUTED law whose witness replays; oracle_mismatch means linked to a hypothesis record.

I18 counts a mutant as killed if 'an outcome moves or a replay disagreement appears'. A replay disagreement is weaker than A1's 'the corresponding obstruction appears', and after faithful re-extraction it signals an extraction defect, not detection. The denominator can also shrink after the fact through 'inside the extracted scope' and the human's equivalent-mutant adjudication.

I1's G9 'complete' means 'validates against the v2 schema the agent wrote'. Ledger completeness is untested: test_no_assumption_outside_cone forbids extra entries only, so dropping an entry passes. Because spec/ledger/assumptions.json entries are keyed by facts_sha256, any re-extraction or --no-registry run silently yields empty model_assumptions.

I4's 'G1 passes after gen/ is regenerated' is tautological, and 'witnesses may change'. Nothing requires gen/M1/model/*.bend to be byte-identical before and after, or each moved def to be proved equal to the old builtin. 'Re-running the 300-trace corpus' cannot detect a semantic change outside the policy's reach.

Most M3 exits are just 'Tests green', with tests written in the same iteration by the same agent (I20–I33, I36, I37). I20's exit passes even if zero M0 laws are re-derived. I39 ('converged = true, or lists the open findings'), I40 ('blind_agreement computed', no threshold, no protocol for what is redone blind), I42 ('manifest validates') and I45 (ablations may be 'not run') can always be satisfied.

The plan inherits M1's misuse of the name HypZ. Whitepaper §8.5 and Appendix D define HypZ as the compression-codec hypothesis ∀x, k ≤ K. Dec(Enc x ++ 0^k) = x. The check 0x01 ‖ sha256(0xc0 ‖ 0^47)[1:] == ZERO_VERSIONED_HASH (I2's holon/oracles/hypz.py, I1's ledger entry 'HypZ (param Z)') is D2. I32's HypZ_rt and HypZ_len then collide with it. Separately, ZERO_VERSIONED_HASH is at Rollup.sol:25, not :24 as docs/M1_REPORT.md:108 says.

I13 predicts that v2 inputs disagree. Per-edge refinement compares a model edge with its own implementation, and a faithful enc_go_v1 writes byte 0 = 1 exactly as Go does, so v2 inputs agree. The O2 difference is enc_sol versus enc_go, a PAR obstruction, not a refinement disagreement. Decoder-domain agreement versus O1 has the same mix-up.
§1.2 row 5.6 says SORT laws only check reachability of reason code 16. L_tag_BVH (rule SORT, subform ghost_tag) checks the tags_ok observer, not a reason code.

§1.2 says only F4 and F6 of Appendix A are fully reproduced. F5's O19 part (L_sym_omega) and F12.1/F12.2 (L_dom_hdr, L_par_hdr_v2) are also reproduced and replayed. The count is a judgment, and I3 then preregisters it as if it were a computed fact.
I8's 'weakening impossible by construction' is false, because laws/M*/REGISTRY.json are agent-written and absent from FROZEN.sha256 (tools/freeze.py FROZEN_ROOTS covers only laws/M0).
agents_md_risks: I5's ∃ counter-laws ('∀ over a finite bounded strategy space, scope bounded(H)') would be recorded as REFUTED. The negation of the frozen ∃σ.P(σ) is ∀σ.¬P(σ) over the full domain; a bounded ∀ is not a counter-law to the frozen statement, and Thm 6.17 defines refutation only for ∀-laws. Calling it REFUTED breaks rule 6 and amounts to rule-2 weakening, since it restates the claim as bounded. Such a result must be UNKNOWN (bounded), or a ∀¬P proof from a generator such as a blocking invariant.

SPLIT as an outcome (I21's split status, I33's 'O8 SPLIT on HypC'). Rule 6 allows exactly PROVED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, and the frozen schemas/result_record.schema.json status enum has no SPLIT; G9 requires v1 validation. A split must be two laws, each with a standard status, under different hypothesis premises.

I7's primary Lean route, bv_decide, introduces an extra axiom; I verified this locally with Lean 4.34.0. A bv_decide proof's #print axioms lists 't1._native.bv_decide.ax_1_5' alongside propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. That fails the plan's own invariant 5 and Lean-G3 audit, and §8.5's 'no axioms'. I7 must use decide or rfl, or per-cell lemmas, from the start.

I6 has generated proofs import ../../core/LAWS.bend. Probe p03 shows that a law with no def is an open claim. So either every importing proof fails with 'TODO found', or, if Bend does not check imported laws, proofs can use unproved core laws as axioms: a rule-3 escape hatch that G5 would not see. The core PROOF must be in each checked closure, and this needs a probe. Separately, frozen tests/test_30_m0_results.py runs `holon run --gen-dir <tmp>/gen` and re-checks proofs in place, so ../../core resolves to <tmp>/core, outside the requested gen dir.

I2's NONVAC.bend holds a law and its proof in one file. That breaks 'Use LAWS.bend for claims and PROOF.bend for proofs', and BEND_PRIMER §4 notes that Bend refuses a PROOF.bend sitting beside a LAWS.bend without importing it. Put each inhabitant in a nonvac/ subdirectory with its own LAWS.bend and PROOF.bend.

I25's realize(d, pf) and as_member(x, ?tag_proof). §7.8 writes these with holes, and rule 3 forbids holes even temporarily. An unprovable coercion inside the model also makes the whole model fail to check, which turns every law importing it UNKNOWN. The plan gives no hole-free encoding, for example the coercion proof as a per-site law premise, or a Maybe-returning realize paired with a site law.

Weakening through new law ids. I20–I29 re-derive analogues of M0/M1 laws under new ids in laws/M3, with added premises (I21's L_fact_Z gains CF and HypZ), Reach restrictions, or bounded scope. STATEMENT_DIFF and A3 (I8) track hash changes per existing id only, so a cross-milestone weakening never passes through the signed-weakening channel (rule 2). Each back-test pair should require a checked S_new ⇒ S_old or a signed weakening entry.

I32's fallback, 'state the law at size N and witness it at N = 4096', restates the claim after seeing kernel limits (rule 2). O4's panic is tied to element index 3968, so a scaled-down N cannot witness it without re-parametrizing that constant.

I4 moves semantics (agg, hdr_of, tags_exact, es_*, the full Go growth table) into lib files outside the IR 0.2 statement hash. That changes the meaning of frozen M1 statements without any hash change, a rule-2 hazard. The full size-class table is the known trigger of the bend2/BendTT mismatch (docs/M1_REPORT.md §2.6, replay/M1/kernel_mismatch/), so L_own_txspayload's dual-kernel status is at risk too.

M3 hand-writes facts (I23, I29, I30, I31, I32, I33) after M2 built extractors. That violates AGENTS rule 4 ('generate, don't hand-write') in spirit and the whitepaper's 'hand-written allowed until M2' (App H, §15.3).

Conflicts with frozen tests. (a) I10's evidence-derived default triage (E6 → intent_question) and I34's intended_bounded could change record triage. Frozen tests/test_30 asserts M0 triage equals predictions/M0.json (L_par_hdr_ssvh: intent_question), and tests_m1/test_m1_results.py asserts M1 triage equals spec/M1/predictions.json. intended_bounded is not in the frozen triage enum, and invariant 9 forbids rewriting tests_m1. (b) Every new gate check (G6, G9, G11V, GEVID, G8, G10, Lean G7, G1 over records) must pass on the M0 copy in tests/test_40_gate.py. copy_repo drops .git, so no check may depend on git, and run_holon has an 1800 s timeout that Lean, G11V and record regeneration could exceed; copy_repo also copies build/ and any lean/.lake.

The tamper-resistance claims rest on files the agent can write: results/quarantine.json, laws/M*/REGISTRY.json, holon/statement_diff.py and tests_m2's prereg-order test. Until Q1 freezes them, these protections are self-certified.
AGENTS 'Read first' item 3 says to read 'the prompt for your session, in prompts/'. The plan's session protocol reads a section of the plan instead, and creates no prompts/ files for I1–I49.

AGENTS rule 4 ('proofs come from proof generators') conflicts with whitepaper §10.4 (agents fill the remaining goals) and with I36's hand-proved Graph, Walk and holonomy theorems kept in a 'catalog', which are hand-written proofs. Q14 asks only about the core lemma library, not about meta-theorem proofs or an agent-proof intake.

Hygiene (rule 8; frozen tests/test_12_hygiene.py scans the whole repo for .env and bunfig.toml). I15's vendor/ fallback, any in-repo node_modules for the Solidity harnesses (I13/I14), and the I43 baseline installs must be checked: a single .env in a vendored tree fails GENV and the frozen test.

If test_prereg_order.py skips when .git is absent (shallow CI clones, copy_repo), that is 'make tests skip', which rule 2 forbids. It must fail instead, or be scoped explicitly as a non-gate audit tool.
